title: The Parks crew leader whose good attitude is contagious
excerpt: Skip Brown greets residents with a smile and isn't too proud to empty a trash can. A neighbor says he's the best of Rowlett.
body:
Most of us never think about the people who make a city event run smoothly. One Rowlett resident noticed, and thought he deserved a thank-you.

Skip Brown is a Parks Maintenance Crew Leader for the City of Rowlett. Over several weeks this year, a resident watched him at work around town, and kept seeing the same thing: a professional who takes pride in how he does his job and how he treats people.

At Live on Main in downtown Rowlett on June 5, Skip greeted residents with a warm welcome that set the tone for the whole evening. Later that night, he spotted a full trash can and emptied it himself, without being asked and without a second thought. It's a small thing, but it's the kind of small thing that shows who someone is.

The resident was impressed enough to send a formal commendation to the director of the Parks Department. "Mr. Brown embodies the spirit of service that defines the best of Rowlett staff," they wrote. His positive attitude and leadership by example, they added, "are not only commendable, but contagious."

The next time you're at a Rowlett park or a downtown event, look for the people in the city shirts keeping everything running. And if you see Skip, tell him thanks.
